description: Second OCR engine (EasyOCR) vs Tesseract v4_psm3 on the ContextRico-DP DEV/TEST split of ml/eval_screenshots.py, with the current text model and the same image-level decision rule. Operating points are picked on DEV only; TEST is reported.

craft_mlt_25k.pth.role: CRAFT text detector (Clova AI, MIT-licensed code/model, redistributed by EasyOCR)

provenance.tesseract: pytesseract + system Tesseract (unchanged); OCR cache from ml/eval_screenshots.py (v4_psm3)

dataset.name: ContextRico-DP
dataset.negatives_note: Negatives are ContextRico images with NO text-observable label. They are still dark-pattern UIs of visual types (Hard to Close, Nagging, Default Choice, False Hierarchy, ...) and some may contain unlabelled urgency/scarcity/social-proof or confirmshaming text, so the 'flag rate on negatives' (and hence image-level false positives / precision) is an UPPER bound on true false alarms.

decision_rule: ml/eval_screenshots.metrics: image flagged if any candidate has p_dark >= tau
selection_rule: On DEV only, evaluate every (config, tau) with tau in {text-model threshold} U {0.3..0.9 step 0.05}. Admissible points have negative-image flag rate <= 0.15. Choose the admissible point with the highest image-level F1; points within 0.01 F1 of the best are tied and broken by higher category-correct recall, then by the text model's own threshold, then by lower OCR s/image. If an admissible point at the text model's own threshold is within 0.02 F1 of the best, it is preferred (no OCR-specific threshold unless it clearly helps). If no point is admissible, the lowest neg flag rate wins.

timing_controlled_subsample.note: sequential, one image at a time, warm models, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 (set by ml/__init__ for the torch+xgboost segfault), so EasyOCR-CPU uses one intra-op thread

synthetic_screens.source: PNG files saved by ml/benchmark_intelligence.py (exp_B_screenshots); texts from intelligence_benchmark.json
synthetic_screens.match_rule: read = some OCR candidate matches the rendered text with difflib ratio >= 0.85 after lower-casing and removing non-alphanumerics (same rule as benchmark B)
synthetic_screens.S1_S3_decline_style: S1/S2: 15px rgb(170,170,170) on white; S3: 13px rgb(190,190,190) on white

caveats: mean_ocr_seconds_per_image in the metric blocks is NOT comparable across engines: Tesseract times come from the eval_screenshots cache (6 concurrent processes), EasyOCR times are sequential on mps, union = sum. Use timing_controlled_subsample for speed. (The selection rule only uses s/image as the last tie-break.)
ocr_confidence is not calibrated across engines (Tesseract: mean word confidence; EasyOCR: recogniser confidence). Nothing in the decision rule uses it.

Negatives are ContextRico images with NO text-observable label. They are still dark-pattern UIs of visual types (Hard to Close, Nagging, Default Choice, False Hierarchy, ...) and some may contain unlabelled urgency/scarcity/social-proof or confirmshaming text, so the 'flag rate on negatives' (and hence image-level false positives / precision) is an UPPER bound on true false alarms.
Small positive sets (DEV 42 / TEST 41 images); see Wilson CIs and paired McNemar p-values.
EasyOCR on the ContextRico set was run on mps; timing_controlled_subsample reports whether CPU and MPS outputs were identical on its images.
